# Updates to the five-MAM-products evacuation plan

State: open, first entry 2026-09-11. Every entry here corrects or supplements
`doc/PLAN-evacuate-five-MAM-products.md` (`State: complete`), which is left exactly as written.

Ben's decision, 2026-09-11: a finished dated document — a review, a remediation plan, a completed
plan, an execution record — is left as written, like a pushed commit. A correction to one goes in
a sibling file named `<stem>-update.md`, which is what this file is for that plan. Nothing here
edits the document it corrects.

## Phase 6's "unchanged generated bytes" describes `40b8ea4b`, not a later tree

Recorded by a Claude session on 2026-09-11, for finding 6 of `doc/review-findings-2026-09-10.md`.
It supplements the passage "The intended Phase 6 result is unchanged generated bytes".

The unchanged generated bytes that the Phase 6 records verify are the state at `40b8ea4b`
(2026-09-10 16:05), and that state lasted hours. The Wikisource cutover
(`doc/PLAN-wikisource-derived-mam-products.md`, commits `426fa229` and `321b2eeb`) and the
production refresh `209b4c05` (2026-09-10 20:53, recorded in
`doc/PLAN-efficient-wikisource-downloads-update.md`) reached `main` after `40b8ea4b`, through the
merge `a0a2e3ab` at 21:22, and changed outputs Phase 6 had verified. Measured by that review at
`0354b6cc`: 97 of the 415 outputs 6B records, 16 of 6C's 99 and 57 of 6D's 295 no longer carry
their recorded Git blobs, each last changed by `209b4c05`, `321b2eeb`, `426fa229`, `8f5c1c96` or
`516a4a1a`, and none of those five commits is an ancestor of `40b8ea4b`
(`git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> 40b8ea4b`). The Phase 6 records are dated and name
`40b8ea4b`, so they are right as written; this entry says only that their "unchanged" describes
that commit and not a later tree. Neither that plan nor the programme mentions the cutover.

## The two bounded public findings are a numbered list

Recorded by Codex on 2026-09-12, for finding 20.4 of
`doc/review-findings-2026-09-10.md`. The passage beginning “The sweep found two bounded public
findings” announces two findings but presents them as “First” and “Second” in running prose. The
passage should be read as this numbered list:

1. The shared Hebrew-prose verification guidance still called landed MAM-OSIS a sibling. The
   tracked guidance, the Claude live copy and the Codex live copy now list all five products
   inside MAM-basics and retain only MAM-private and a temporary redirect-host clone as siblings;
   both required whole-skill comparisons passed with no difference.
2. The manually maintained MAM-with-doc sigil page still linked source issues 6 and 8 and called
   the landed tree a repository. Commit `3e3a93ef82615710a2520bd85a3086e9ae4fbc9d` links open
   MAM-basics issues 257 and 259 and calls the tree a product. Pages run `34523189844` deployed
   that commit successfully; a fresh HTTP request returned 9,613 bytes exactly matching the
   commit, with both current links present and both old links absent.

The completed evacuation plan remains unchanged; this entry corrects only the presentation of its
two findings.
